summary: Isomer's SwiftUI, on wasm (the web) and Android (and Linux and Windows), is the SwiftUI app code is written against, drawn by each platform's renderer (React, Jetpack Compose, or Isomer's own GPU renderer). It covers the everyday core: stacks, lists and forms, text and images, the common controls, navigation stacks and split views, tabs, toolbars, sheets and alerts, state and environment, Observation. docs/swiftui_api_audit.md goes through the gaps area by area, with priorities. On Apple platforms an app uses Apple's SwiftUI.
deviations: Behavior the renderers cannot yet give is accepted and ignored or approximated (docs/swiftui_api_audit.md, section 5): `.transition` is accepted but not animated, springs are ease-outs, `GeometryProxy.frame(in:)` is relative to the view.

newer.title: New in iOS 27
newer.intent: planned, as the rest of the interface is

groups.title: UIKit and AppKit
groups.why: Interop with UIKit and AppKit (representables, hosting controllers and views, app delegates, UIKit and AppKit types in signatures). Isomer's platforms have neither; Isomer's own `PlatformViewRepresentable` embeds a platform view instead.

groups.title: Combine
groups.why: SwiftUI's side of Combine: `ObservableObject` models (`@StateObject`, `@ObservedObject`, `@EnvironmentObject`, `.environmentObject(_:)`) and publishers (`onReceive`). Combine is kept for backward compatibility; Isomer's apps use Observation (`@Observable` with `@State`, `@Environment(Model.self)`, `.environment(_:)` and `@Bindable`) and Swift concurrency (2026-10-12).

groups.title: Core Data
groups.why: Fetch requests and results are Core Data's, which Isomer does not provide (an app's data on the device is SQLite's, through swift_sql).

groups.title: Apple platform features
groups.why: Features of Apple's platforms themselves: widgets and Live Activities, App Intents, StoreKit, Apple Pencil, visionOS spaces and ornaments, watchOS and tvOS input, Handoff, menu bar extras, Writing Tools, document launch screens.

groups.title: Accessibility
groups.why: The accessibility modifiers, rotors and technologies.

groups.title: Shaders, drawing and rendering
groups.intent: planned (shader effects with Isomer's Metal, after 0.31)
groups.why: Shaders and the visual effects that take them, `GraphicsContext`, `Canvas`, mesh gradients, color matrices, `ImageRenderer`.

groups.title: Documents, scenes, windows and commands
groups.why: Scenes beyond `WindowGroup`'s basics (document groups, settings, windows), scene modifiers, menus and keyboard commands.

groups.title: Tables
groups.why: `Table` and its columns and rows.

groups.title: Drag and drop, sharing and the pasteboard
groups.why: Dragging and dropping, `Transferable`-based sharing beyond `ShareLink`'s basics, paste buttons.

groups.title: Gestures
groups.why: Gesture values and their composition beyond tap, drag and magnify.

groups.title: Layout
groups.why: The `Layout` protocol, grids, preferences and anchors, subview collections, alignment guides.

groups.title: Styles
groups.why: The style protocols and their configurations (`ButtonStyle`, `ToggleStyle`, `LabelStyle`, `GaugeStyle`…); Isomer's controls take fixed style options.

groups.title: Animation and transitions
groups.why: Animation curves and springs, `Animatable`, transitions, keyframe and phase animators, matched geometry.

groups.title: Text and fonts
groups.why: Text formatting and attributed text, text selection and input formatting, the rest of `Font` and `Text`'s modifiers.

groups.title: Environment values
groups.why: Environment values Isomer does not set yet.

groups.title: Navigation, tabs and search
groups.why: Value-based navigation (`NavigationPath`, `navigationDestination`), the rest of tabs and tab customization, search suggestions and scopes.

groups.title: Controls
groups.why: The rest of the controls' initializers and modifiers.

groups.title: Scrolling
groups.why: Scroll positions and targets, scroll phases and the rest of the scroll view modifiers.

groups.title: Shapes, colors and geometry
groups.why: The rest of shapes and their transforms, colors and gradients, blend modes, angles and insets.

groups.title: Haptic feedback
groups.why: Sensory feedback (haptics) through each platform.

groups.title: Data flow
groups.why: The rest of the property wrappers and dynamic properties (`Binding`'s and `State`'s less common members, `GestureState`, `FocusedValue`, `SceneStorage`…).

groups.title: View modifiers
groups.why: Other modifiers on `View`.

groups.title: Other declarations
groups.why: The rest of SwiftUI's interface: builders, conditional conformances of `ModifiedContent` and the like, and smaller types.

additions: Isomer's SwiftUI declares nothing Apple's SwiftUI lacks: its interface is a subset of Apple's (iOS's and macOS's), declaration by declaration and type by type (a struct where Apple has a protocol counts as Isomer's own). What Apple's SwiftUI brings along from other frameworks comes from modules of their own (CoreTransferable, re-exported; not Combine, UIKit or Dispatch, whose APIs are for backward compatibility), and Isomer's own additions are the `Isomer` module's (its `Clipboard` among them). Anything listed here is a regression: move it to the Isomer module or an Isomer* library (IsomerSwiftUI for what a host binds), or make it `package` when only Isomer's own modules use it (`@_spi` counts as public).
